title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive from an automated identification system. A license-plate reader misread one character of a plate and returned a match to a stolen vehicle. The alert was then acted on as though it identified a person, rather than as a lead that still had to be checked.

The failure sits at the handoff between the alert and the enforcement action. Catching it would have taken an independent verification of the plate before enforcement, which is what the vendor itself says its alerts require. The sheriff's office instead attributed the error to a tinted plate cover and called the deputy's actions reasonable.

What is not established is whether the plate cover was illegal or caused the misread, because that account comes from the sheriff's office and not from an independent finding. No ruling on the lawfulness of the detention is reported.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was reportedly detained at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office later said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the error and called the deputy’s actions reasonable. Flock said alerts should be independently verified before enforcement.
